name: Louisiana

code.name: Louisiana Revised Statutes, Title 18 (the Louisiana Election Code)
code.edition: as amended through the 2025 First Extraordinary Session, 'January, 2026' printing, published by the Secretary of State from the House of Representatives database
code.site: https://legis.la.gov/ (the legislature's own site: connection reset, not read); text read in the Secretary of State's PDF https://www.sos.la.gov/media/oy5jhnk1/election-code.pdf

la-election-code.note: The legislature's site (legis.la.gov) reset our connection, so the statute text was read in the Secretary of State's own PDF of Title 18 (the whole Election Code, 'As Amended Through the 2025 First Extraordinary Session'). It was found by web search; the two Secretary of State pages checked (elections-voting, election-guides-handbooks) do not link to it. It is the statute's own words but not the legislature's own publication, so it is graded as an agency publication, not as the statute site.

ties.applies_to: the slates of presidential electors, in the general election
ties.steps: if two or more slates with the highest number of votes receive the same number, none is elected; the slate elected is selected by a public drawing of lots by the state board of election supervisors, at the state capitol, within one week after the results become official (R.S. 18:1261(A))
ties.who: the state board of election supervisors

sources.quote: If two or more of the slates of candidates having the highest number of votes receive the same number of votes, none of the slates of candidates is elected, and the slate of candidates elected shall be selected by a public drawing of lots conducted by the state board of election supervisors from among the slate of candidates who received such highest number of votes in the election.

ties.note: R.S. 18:1261(A). Read in the Secretary of State's PDF of Title 18, not on the legislature's site.

ties.applies_to: "an office" in a general election (offices of Congress and all the state's elective offices, other than presidential elector)
ties.steps: the candidates who tied are not elected; the election for the office is 'returned to the people' on the fourth Saturday after the election date at which the tie occurred (R.S. 18:512(C))
ties.who: the voters, at a new election; the section does not say who may stand in it

sources.quote: If, as a result of a tie vote in a general election, the number of candidates who would be elected to an office exceeds the number of persons to be elected to the office, the candidates who received the same number of votes for that office in the general election are not elected. The election for officers thus not elected shall be returned to the people on the fourth Saturday after the election date at which the tie vote occurred.
Primary and general elections are held to elect persons to Congress and to all the elective offices in this state, except the office of presidential elector.

ties.note: R.S. 18:512(C) says "an office" and does not name federal, state or legislative offices; R.S. 18:401(A) says the Title's elections elect "persons to Congress and to all the elective offices in this state", so the rule is read as covering them [inferred from the two sections together]. Congress: R.S. 18:1271 sends US senators and representatives to "this Title for the election of public officers" except as Part II provides, and the Part II sections listed do not mention a tie. The text of the general-election tie rule does not say whether the new election is open to all the tied candidates or to new ones. Read in the Secretary of State's PDF, not on the legislature's site.

ties.applies_to: "an office" in a general election, read as covering parish, municipal, school and district offices (state general law only; home-rule charters and local ordinances were not read)
ties.steps: as for the other offices: the tied candidates are not elected and the election is returned to the people on the fourth Saturday after the election date (R.S. 18:512(C))
ties.who: the voters, at a new election

sources.quote: If, as a result of a tie vote in a general election, the number of candidates who would be elected to an office exceeds the number of persons to be elected to the office, the candidates who received the same number of votes for that office in the general election are not elected. The election for officers thus not elected shall be returned to the people on the fourth Saturday after the election date at which the tie vote occurred.

ties.note: R.S. 18:512(C) says "an office"; reading it as covering local offices rests on R.S. 18:401(A) ("all the elective offices in this state"). Charters were not read.

ties.applies_to: the open ('jungle') primary, for every office that is not a party primary office (statewide offices other than the Supreme Court, BESE and the Public Service Commission, the legislature, parish and local offices)
ties.steps: a tie does not decide the primary by lot: if a tie would send more candidates to the general election than the maximum, all the candidates with the same number of votes qualify for the general election (R.S. 18:483); if a tie would elect more candidates than there are seats, the tied candidates are not elected but qualify as candidates in the general election (R.S. 18:511(D)); a tie in the general election is then settled as above
ties.who: the voters, in the general election

sources.quote: If, as a result of a tie vote in a primary election, the number of candidates who would qualify for the general election is more than twice the number of persons remaining to be elected to the office, all of the candidates who received the same number of votes in the primary election qualify for the general election.

If, as a result of a tie vote in a primary election, the number of candidates who would be elected to an office exceeds the number of persons to be elected to the office, the candidates who received the same majority of the votes cast in the primary election are not elected, but they are qualified as candidates in the general election.

ties.note: R.S. 18:483 and 18:511(D). R.S. 18:2 defines 'primary election' as covering both a party primary office and any other office; this rule is the one for the non-party primary. Read in the Secretary of State's PDF.

ties.applies_to: the closed party primary, for the party primary offices (US Senate and US House, justice of the supreme court, the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education, and the Public Service Commission, as R.S. 18:2 defines them)
ties.steps: a tie for first or second place in the first party primary sends the tied candidates of that party to the second party primary (R.S. 18:410.7(B)(2) and (3)); a tie in the second party primary leaves no nominee, and the party nominee is selected by a public drawing of lots by the State Board of Election Supervisors, at the state capitol, within one week after the results become official (R.S. 18:410.7(C))
ties.who: the State Board of Election Supervisors

sources.quote: In the case of a tie vote in the second party primary of a major political party, none of the candidates qualify as the party nominee for the general election, and the party nominee shall be selected by a public drawing of lots conducted by the State Board of Election Supervisors from among the candidates who received the highest number of votes in the second party primary election.

In the case of a tie vote for first place in the first party primary of a major political party, all of the candidates affiliated with the same political party who received the same highest number of votes qualify for the second party primary.

"Party primary office" means an office of senator or representative in the United States Congress, justice of the supreme court, the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education, and the Public Service Commission.

ties.note: R.S. 18:410.7 and 18:2(9). These closed party primaries are new (Acts 2024, 1st Ex. Sess., No. 1; Acts 2024, No. 640; Acts 2025, No. 386), held on the spring dates under R.S. 18:410.10; no election has yet been held under them in the years the site's history covers. Read in the Secretary of State's PDF.

ties.applies_to: a tie on a ballot proposition
ties.steps: no provision for a tie on a proposition was found
ties.note: The whole text of Title 18 as the Secretary of State prints it was searched for 'tie' and 'equal number'. The hits are R.S. 18:482, 483, 410.7, 511(D), 512(C) and 1261 (offices and slates), R.S. 18:443 (a party's state central committee, by lot) and a presiding officer's casting vote in a local governing body in the section on appointments; none concerns a proposition. Whether the Louisiana Constitution or another Title says what a tied proposition does was not read.

threshold.conditions: the number of absentee by mail and early voting ballots cast for all candidates for the office could make a difference in the outcome of the election for the office
threshold.in_words: no percentage or vote margin; a candidate for the office may have the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots recounted if those ballots could change who wins

who_may_request: a candidate for the office, in writing, filed with the clerk of court by 4:30 p.m. on the third calendar day after the election
recounts.cost_bearer: the requesting candidate, who pays all reasonable costs when the request is filed; the clerk refunds the costs if the recount changes the outcome of the election, and they become a reimbursable election expense

sources.quote: if the number of absentee by mail and early voting ballots cast for all candidates for an office could make a difference in the outcome of the election for the office, upon the written request of a candidate for the office, the board shall recount the absentee by mail ballots by hand or scanning equipment and early voting ballots electronically
The candidate or the voter in the proposition election requesting the recount shall be responsible for all reasonable costs associated with such recount, which shall be payable to the clerk of court.

recounts.note: R.S. 18:1313.1(K)(2) in the current text (the same words are in R.S. 18:1313(K)(2), the alternative procedure a parish board may elect). Only the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots are recounted under it; ballots cast on election day are on voting machines, which a candidate may have reopened for reinspection on written request at the candidate's cost (R.S. 18:573(A)(3)), and that is an inspection, not a recount. The statute names 'an office' and does not separate federal, state and local offices, so the kinds are read from that wording [inferred]. The whole of Title 18 as printed was searched for 'recount': there is no automatic recount and no recount keyed to a percentage or number of votes.

threshold.conditions: the number of absentee by mail and early voting ballots cast for and against the proposition could make a difference in the outcome of the election
threshold.in_words: no percentage or vote margin; a person who voted in the proposition election may have the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots recounted if those ballots could change the outcome

who_may_request: a person who voted in the proposition election, in writing, filed with the clerk of court by 4:30 p.m. on the third calendar day after the election
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, who pays all reasonable costs when the request is filed; refunded if the recount changes the outcome of the election

sources.quote: if the number of absentee by mail and early voting ballots cast for and against a proposition could make a difference in the outcome of the election, upon the written request of a person who voted in the proposition election, the board shall recount the absentee by mail ballots by hand or scanning equipment and early voting ballots electronically

recounts.note: R.S. 18:1313.1(K)(2)(a)(ii) and (d). Same limits as the rule for offices: only the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots.

threshold.conditions: the party alleges an error in the counting of the absentee by mail and early voting ballots that would have changed the outcome of the election
threshold.in_words: no margin; before the trial of an election contest a party to the suit may move for a recount of the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots on alleging a counting error that would have changed the outcome

who_may_request: a party to an election-contest suit, by ex parte motion before the trial
recounts.cost_bearer: the party who demanded the recount, if the court finds the original count correct or the error would not have changed the result; otherwise no party

sources.quote: Prior to the trial of an election contest, a party to the suit by ex parte motion may seek a recount of the absentee by mail and early voting ballots if he alleges that there is an error in the counting of the absentee by mail and early voting ballots which would have changed the outcome of the election.

if the court determines that the original count of the absentee by mail and early voting ballots was correct or that the error would not have changed the result of the election, the cost of recounting shall be assessed against the party who demanded the recount.

recounts.note: R.S. 18:1451 and 18:1452, in the part on recounts of absentee and early ballots in contests. Recorded because the Title puts it under 'recount'; the contest chapters themselves were not otherwise read.

notes: Every quotation was read in the Secretary of State's PDF of Title 18 (sos.la.gov), because legis.la.gov reset the connection; the grade is therefore 'agency publication', not 'statute site', and the orchestrator may set it aside. The PDF prints the Title as amended through the 2025 First Extraordinary Session, with 'January, 2026' page footers.

Louisiana has two systems at once since 2026: closed party primaries (with a second party primary) for Congress, the supreme court, BESE and the Public Service Commission, and the open primary followed by a general election for every other office. A tie rule is recorded for each.

Louisiana has no automatic recount and no margin-triggered recount in Title 18 as printed; a candidate (or, for a proposition, a voter) may ask for a recount of the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots only, at their own cost, when those ballots could change the result.
